notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one
notes.generation: 4: introduced 1997 (weapons.ibx's generation 4 = from 1995); a SAM's generation keys only its weapons.ibx section
notes.kg: the upper end of the PMU-2 column's 330–1,900 kg (the 330 kg is the 9M96 missile, inferred)
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter of strength 300 (our damage scale, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; held by blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead (docs/real-weapons.md §1.4) times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (180 kg)
notes.speed_ms: the 48N6's 1,900 m/s from the variant table, which the article marks less reliable
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion._spiralAccelBeta: top speed a / beta: 120 / the top speed
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the missile's launch zone from rest (combat.gd fires from the unit's pose at speed 0; missile.rs dlz with "burn": the distance travelled in burn + 4 s) is its published range
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)

footnotes.w-s300: Wikipedia, "S-300 missile system" (PMU-2: 3–200 km, 0.01–27 km, 1,900 m/s, 30N6E2 I/J band, 64N6E2 search, 12 TELs, 3 s launch interval; comparison table PMU-2 column: missile mass 330–1,900 kg, warhead 180 kg; the table's figures are "less reliable") (read 2026-11-03), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-300_missile_system
footnotes.ds-aim9: designation-systems.net, "Raytheon AIM-9 Sidewinder" (AIM-9A / B effective kill radius about 9 m), https://www.designation-systems.net/dusrm/m-9.html
